issues.description: Deprecation message has a typo: 'stlib' instead of 'stdlib'
issues.detail: The docstring's `.. deprecated:: 4.3` block says 'Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`...'. That's 'stlib', not 'stdlib'. This will render in the published docs. Fix the typo. One-line change. Don't ship typos in user-facing deprecation copy.

issues.description: Import order in tests/test_cmd_inspect_app.py violates isort/PEP8 conventions used elsewhere in the file
issues.detail: `import contextlib` got slotted between `from argparse import Namespace` and `import io`. The surrounding code groups `from` imports separately from plain `import` statements. If the project runs isort (it does — falcon uses ruff/isort in tox), this will either get auto-fixed or fail the lint job. Either run the formatter or place the import correctly. Match the codebase's voice; don't make the maintainer fix your import order.

issues.description: Test doesn't verify the captured-by-contextlib path also works — only that the deprecated path still functions
issues.detail: `test_deprecated_redirected` confirms the warning fires and that the old code still works. Fine. But the entire claim of this patch is 'contextlib does the same thing,' and there's no test asserting parity. A one-liner asserting `contextlib.redirect_stdout` produces the same captured output would close the loop. Not blocking — the stdlib carries its own tests — but if you're going to add a test, add the one that proves your rationale.

review.summary: Small, well-scoped deprecation patch. Three things: deprecation decorator, docstring directive, news fragment, and call-site migrations in the one internal test file that used it. The diff does one thing, the commit message tells you why, and the scope is right — this is what a good deprecation patch looks like. Issues are minor: a 'stlib' typo in the user-facing deprecation copy, suspicious import ordering in the test file that the project's linter will likely flag, and a missing parity test that would actually demonstrate the rationale. Fix the typo, run the formatter, and this lands. NEEDS-WORK on the typo alone; the rest is taste. GOOD-TASTE for deleting a special-case utility in favor of the stdlib general case.
